# UseCaseDefinition <span class="sd-sphinx-override sd-badge sd-outline-primary sd-text-primary">SysML</span><a href="#usecasedefinition-sysml" class="headerlink" title="Link to this heading"><span class="nerd-font"></span></a>

*<span class="pre">class</span><span class="w"> </span>*<span class="sig-name descname"><span class="pre">UseCaseDefinition</span></span><a href="#syside.UseCaseDefinition" class="headerlink" title="Link to this definition"><span class="nerd-font"></span></a>  
Implementation of <span class="pre">`UseCaseDefinition`</span> defined in the SysML specification.

**Specification**:

> <div>
>
> A <span class="pre">`UseCaseDefinition`</span> is a <span class="pre">`CaseDefinition`</span> that specifies a set of actions performed by its subject, in interaction with one or more actors external to the subject. The objective is to yield an observable result that is of value to one or more of the actors.
>
> </div>

For language description, see section <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Release/refs/tags/2025-07/doc/2a-OMG_Systems_Modeling_Language.pdf#page=179" class="reference external" target="_blank">7.25.2</a> of the SysML specification. For more details on the model, see section <a href="https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Systems-Modeling/SysML-v2-Release/refs/tags/2025-07/doc/2a-OMG_Systems_Modeling_Language.pdf#page=413" class="reference external" target="_blank">8.3.25.3</a> of the SysML specification.
